headline: DeepMind SynthID Bio watermarks AI-designed proteins; BWI IT outage cuts ~60k Reservisten off systems; Cariad eyes ~1,000 more cuts; Gemini Skills replace Gems

stories.title: DeepMind introduces SynthID Bio — watermarks for AI-designed proteins
facts: DeepMind (Sep 30): SynthID Bio embeds an imperceptible, verifiable watermark into AI-generated protein sequences and predicted 3D structures — detectable on the synthesized physical protein, not just the digital model.
Wet-lab: watermarked binders (AlphaProteo + SynthID-enabled ProteinMPNN) matched hit rate, affinity, and sequence diversity vs unwatermarked across VEGF-A, SARS-CoV-2 spike RBD, and PD-L1.
Also fine-tunes part of AlphaFold 3’s diffusion network so predicted coordinates carry a detectable signature while preserving accuracy.
Publishing methods paper + open-sourcing code/in-vitro data/weights (Nature DOI 10.1038/s41586-026-10965-y). Framed as one biosecurity layer for synthesis screening — not a silver bullet.
stories.whyItMatters: First major lab demo that an AI protein design can stay functional while carrying a machine-readable provenance signal — relevant as generative bio tools scale and synthesis screeners lose the ‘unknown = natural’ assumption.

image.alt: Visualization of a watermarked VEGF-A protein binder with SynthID Bio signal

stories.title: BWI IT outage: ~60k Reservisten cut off from Bundeswehr systems for a week+
facts: Handelsblatt / MoD: roughly 60,000 non-active Reservisten have had no access to BWI workstations, Bundeswehr email, and the messenger for more than a week.
MoD: operational causes, not a cyberattack — “no data exfiltration or third-party access.” BWI cites update-related impairment; working to restore access “soon.”
Bundeswehr circles (via Handelsblatt): mass data import during system updates allegedly deleted records for non-called-up Reservisten — described as a catastrophe in a defense scenario.
stories.whyItMatters: Even without a breach, losing reserve connectivity for a week exposes how brittle command-and-control IT is when updates and imports go wrong.

image.alt: Bundeswehr soldier working at a laptop

stories.title: VW’s Cariad plans ~1,000 more job cuts (~¼ of remaining staff)
facts: Handelsblatt (via heise): Cariad told staff at a Wed Betriebsversammlung it plans ~1,000 further cuts — about a quarter of ~4,300 remaining employees after last year’s ~1,600 cuts.
Timing/instruments still open; worker negotiations not started. Rationale cited: stay competitive vs external software vendors; also reviewing AI efficiency.
Internal paper (HB): cut investments ~€6.1B for 2027–2031 and contribute another ~€400M to group EBIT by early next decade; concept due by end-Dec 2026.
~500 roles tied to the ended Bosch “Automated Driving Alliance” are especially under pressure. Cariad also reportedly cancelled several Tarifverträge (VW cancelled many group contracts the same day).
stories.whyItMatters: Confirms Cariad’s shift from sole group software-platform builder to a smaller integrator/maintainer under harsh cost targets — more German auto-software jobs at risk.

stories.title: Gemini rolls out Skills globally — Gems to be replaced
facts: Google (Sep 30): Skills land in Gemini chat globally (18+; AI subscription tiers) — save reusable instructions, invoke with `/skill-name`, stack multiple skills, attach reference files (txt/PDF/images).
Skills already in Gemini Spark; Workspace business/enterprise/nonprofit/edu follow in coming weeks.

Gems sunset: Nov 2026 for personal accounts; Mar 2027 Workspace biz/enterprise/nonprofit; Jun 2027 education — auto-migrate Gems → Skills. Opal mini-apps experiment also turns down with personal Gems.
stories.whyItMatters: Google is consolidating custom assistants onto a slash-command skills model and sunsetting Gems on a published timetable.
